title: Changing the Proofing Pathway on a Claimant Identity Verification Case
content:
A claimant may move a Claimant Identity Verification case to another pathway, for example from online proofing to an American Job Center visit after failed selfie matches.

## Rule

1. A pathway change is accepted only while the case status is opened or failed. The status is taken from the case record before the change is made.
2. A failed case may change pathway only where the failed pathway allows a change after failure; the Identity Theft Victim Re-Verification pathway never changes once failed, and such a case is handed to the fraud unit.
3. After a change on a failed case the case resumes in progress on the new pathway; attempts, appointments and documents on the old pathway do not count toward the new pathway's limits, while documents already accepted remain accepted where the new pathway accepts that document type and form.
4. A change never restarts the verification deadline.

## Questions answered by the rule

**Can a case that stands in progress change pathway?**
No. A change is accepted only while the case is opened or failed; a case in progress, verified, expired, fraud confirmed or closed is outside that condition.

**Can an opened case change pathway before any work starts?**
Yes. Opened is one of the two statuses in which a change is accepted.

**What does a failed case need besides the failed status?**
The pathway on which it failed must allow a change after failure. A case that failed on Identity Theft Victim Re-Verification never changes pathway, and it is handed to the fraud unit.

**What status does the case take after the change?**
A failed case that changes pathway resumes in progress on the new pathway.

**Do the old pathway's failed attempts or missed appointments count on the new pathway?**
No. Attempts, appointments and documents on the old pathway do not count toward the new pathway's limits.

**What happens to documents already accepted?**
They remain accepted where the new pathway accepts that document type and form. For example (hypothetical), an original Social Security card accepted as a secondary document on one pathway remains accepted after a move to another pathway that accepts a Social Security card as a secondary document in original form.

**Does the deadline start again?**
No. The verification deadline stays where it was before the change.
